title: Reachability of an exocoetid-like glider from a halfbeak-like ancestor (model escape-fitness landscape)
evidence_kind: simulated: model output under declared assumptions; not an observation of any fish, predator or lineage

model.name: claude-eco reachability/1: 4-trait landscape (pectoral length/SL, fin aspect ratio, mass, hypocaudal share) -> project point-mass glide -> escape probability; maximin accessible path, Lande walk, straight line
model.context: Asks whether, under a stated escape-fitness function, a monotonically improving path exists from a halfbeak-like ancestor (Daane 2021 S1A Hyporhamphus proportions) to an Exocoetus-like exocoetid (Daane 2021 S1A, Fish 1990, FishBase). Airborne phase uses the project's own glide model. SIMULATION; reachability in a model is not evidence that the transition happened or how.

findings: ANSWER (default physics, H_vis + H_chase): changing all four traits together along the straight line ancestor -> target, W never decreases (max drop 0.0e+00 over 200 steps) -- a monotonically improving path EXISTS when traits co-vary. With one trait changing at a time there is no strictly improving path: the least-bad route dips by 1.2e-04.

With an aquatic fin cost the co-varying straight line stays monotone in 0 of 3 H_vis+H_chase rows (kappa_fin 0.1: max drop 2.6e-05, 0.3: max drop 1.7e-04, 1.0: max drop 6.9e-04); the ANSWER above is for escape-only fitness and a fixed exit speed (V_exit) shared by all phenotypes.

Default physics, H_vis + H_chase: W rises from 0.484 (ancestor) to 0.9997 (target). The best single-trait path has worst step dW = -1.21e-04: no strictly improving path; every path crosses a dip of at least 1.21e-04. Bottleneck step: M 0.0271 -> 0.033 (dW -1.21e-04).

H_chase only (escape requires out-running the predator's chase): the ancestor's 0.137 pectoral ratio gives a leap shorter than the chase, W = e_swim exactly, and the landscape is flat around it: worst step 0.00e+00; the Lande walk does not move (ends at p = 0.137). Under this hypothesis the model walk's first steps are neutral: in the model, only drift or an additional benefit could start it.
H_vis only: worst step -1.47e-03; bottleneck M 0.0182 -> 0.0222 (dW -1.47e-03).

Selection-driven (Lande) walk, default, H_vis + H_chase, 20000 generations at CV_A 0.05: ends at p = 0.312, A = 1.87, M = 17.0 g, c = 0.635; normalised distance to the Exocoetus-like target 0.87. The walk does not head to the target's aspect ratio or mass under this fitness.
Across all 90 sensitivity rows: strictly improving path in 1, neutral-only in 24, a required dip in 65; the Lande walk came within 0.05 (normalised) of the target in 0.

Where the dip is (reach_post, default landscape): vis: to the target cell worst step -1.5e-03 (M), mass free -7.9e-04 (A), mass frozen -1.3e-03 (p); both: to the target cell worst step -1.2e-04 (M), mass free -2.0e-05 (M), mass frozen -5.7e-05 (p). So the dip is not only the mass increase: in the model, escape probability peaks when the fins first carry the full body weight at water exit (lift ratio phi = 1, pectoral length about 0.3 SL) and declines slightly as fin length p and aspect ratio A rise further toward the exocoetid values.

H_chase plateau: 28912 grid cells connected to the ancestor have W exactly equal to e_swim (up to p = 0.79); a path to the target exists with no downhill step but begins with neutral steps only -- in the H_chase model, selection alone cannot start the walk.

BOTTLENECK of the selection-driven walk: across all 30 H_vis+H_chase rows the walk ends at p = 0.22-0.73 and fin aspect ratio A = 1.59-2.54 (target A = 8.7), never within 0.05 of the target. The stall is where the fins first carry the full weight at water exit; it is robust to the CL control rule (scheduled-CL variant ends at p = 0.36) but not to exit speed (V_exit = 4 m/s: p = 0.73).

Straight-line (traits co-varying) check across the 78 sensitivity rows that ran it: monotone non-decreasing in 54; largest single drop among the rest 6.9e-03. Required single-trait dips, where present, range 5.4e-07 to 5.3e-03 in W per attack; whether drift or a correlated response would cross them depends on effective population size (Ne) and the genetic covariance matrix (G), which this model does not estimate. The Ne needed for selection to dominate at the weakest positive step is given per row in sensitivity.json.
Zero-lift control: ancestor airborne 6.12 m with lift vs 5.24 m ballistic; target 37.7 m vs 12.9 m.
parameter_unknowns: a_LW = 0.00632 g cm^-3: FishBase Hyporhamphus LW used for the whole walk (body shape is not an evolving trait here)
w_body_frac = 0.1 1: body width / SL for span; assumption
V_exit = 10.0 m/s: water-exit speed, same for all phenotypes; Fish 1990 citing Shoulejkin gives ~10 m/s before taxiing (secondary)
dV_taxi = 8.0 m/s: max taxi speed gain at full asymmetry and full aerodynamic support; 10 -> 18 m/s midpoint of Fish 1990/Shoulejkin 16-20
h0 = 0.05 m: height at water exit; assumption
gam0_deg = 15.0 deg: exit angle above horizontal; assumption
e_swim = 0.3 1: escape probability of a prey that does not leave the water, per attack; assumption
U_burst = 10.0 m/s: predator burst speed; inside FishBase Thunnus albacares burst rows 5.21-20.46 m/s
t_burst = 2.0 s: predator burst endurance; assumption
U_sus = 0.56 m/s: predator sustained speed; FishBase Coryphaena hippurus sustained row
d_gap = 3.0 m: H_chase: distance scale over which a lead beyond the predator's chase breaks pursuit; assumption
d_vis = 20.0 m: H_vis: distance scale over which an airborne excursion breaks visual tracking (inf = off); assumption
beta_air = 0.0 1/s: aerial predator hazard while airborne; assumption
p_max = 0.79 1: Davenport 1992 limit on pectoral length / SL
n_trim = 1.0 1: CL rule: commanded lift at exit <= n_trim x weight (1.0 = level at exit); 1.5 lets fast fish climb (argon review)
kappa_fin = 0.0 1: aquatic cost of fins: survival/fecundity factor exp(-kappa_fin * fin wetted area / body wetted area); 0 = escape-only fitness; added after argon review
k_wet = 0.4 1: body wetted area = k_wet SL^2 (ASSUMPTION for a slender fusiform fish)
does_not_establish: that flying fish evolved from a halfbeak-like ancestor along this or any path (phylogeny is from Lovejoy 2004; the path is a model)
that water-exit speed is the same for a halfbeak-like and an exocoetid-like body (V_exit is a shared assumption; 4 m/s is a sensitivity row)
that the walk's stall near p 0.3 explains flying halfbeaks (Oxyporhamphus p = 0.337 in Daane S1A) -- a numerical coincidence in a model, not evidence
that predator escape was the selective agent
real fitness: no fecundity, foraging or development term; fin cost only as a swept factor
the evolution of aspect ratio or mass: the fitness used does not favour the target's A or M
anything about developmental feasibility (that is the developmental scale)
aerodynamics beyond a point-mass glide with a design-assumed polar and no ground effect
open_questions: Which ecological term (ground effect, re-launch/taxi bouts, aerial predators, swimming cost) would make the exocoetid A and M uphill?
Is the H_chase plateau real: do predators keep tracking a short leap?
caption: Reachability on a MODEL escape-fitness landscape. SIMULATION, not an observation; a reachable model path is not evidence the transition happened.
